Subject: Post-demo: FinTechCo performance recap & SLO checklist

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time to demo last week — great conversation. Per our call, attaching a concise SLO checklist and a short recap of the performance numbers we showed. High level: we validated streaming, measured stable P95 latency in our hosted demo environment, and exercised a 50rps burst for the combining-parsing workload you described.

Quick summary (see attached checklist for details):
- Target P95 latency: <= 250ms for short-text generation (<=512 tokens)
- Sustained throughput: ~40–60 requests/sec per dedicated GPU pool for the model variant we demoed
- Concurrent sessions: concurrent streaming sessions tested up to 120 with graceful tail-latency degradation
- Streaming: server-side streaming supported; we validated chunked tokens via our streaming API

Next steps we recommended on the call:
1) Confirm the P95 target and representative test prompts you want us to validate in a pilot.
2) Provide a short list of safety/throughput test cases (security/SRE will run).
3) Agree on pilot scope & timeline (we suggested a 2-week pilot to validate SLOs on your workload).

Attachments: FinTechCo-SLO-checklist-20260610.pdf (SLO table + test vectors)

I'll loop Rishi and Vivek for technical follow-ups; happy to set up a separate SRE session if Priya wants one.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Redwood Inference

Marissa — thanks, this is very helpful. A couple clarifying questions from our SRE/product side before we lock the pilot scope: 

1) Can you confirm the P99 numbers you measured during the demo environment? P95 is useful but we need P99 tail behavior for UX-sensitive flows.
2) For throughput, when you say 40–60 rps per GPU pool, is that single-model throughput or does that assume batching and KV-cache warm? What should we expect for cold-starts?
3) Streaming: do you provide per-token latency guarantees with streaming enabled, or only overall response-time SLOs? Our UI relies on steady chunk pacing.

Priya (cc) — would you be able to join a 30–45m technical sync with Rishi and Vivek tomorrow or Friday? We want to run through exact test prompts and the SRE checklist.

Thanks,
Alex

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: FinTechCo performance recap & SLO checklist

Alex — quick answers to your questions, plus a short runbook for the pilot. TL;DR: P99 tail is higher but within expected ranges; streaming provides per-chunk latency typically <50ms once the stream starts. Full details below.

P99 & tail latency:
- Demo env (warm caches, steady batching): P99 observed ~420–480ms for the 0–512 token prompts we demoed.
- Cold-starts: first-request cold-starts (model load) can be 2–6s depending on model size and whether a pinned instance is available; for pilot we recommend pinning a small dedicated pool to eliminate cold-starts.

Throughput assumptions:
- 40–60 rps is conservative for the model/quantization profile we used with continuous batching and KV cache warm. That assumes small to medium prompts (<=512 tokens).
- With heavier prompts (>=1k tokens) throughput drops ~30–40% due to longer decode times.
- Autoscaling can add burst capacity; recommend sizing pilot for expected sustained plus 2x burst.

Concurrency & stream behavior:
- We validated ~120 concurrent streaming sessions with degraded but acceptable tail latencies; beyond ~200 concurrent streams you’ll see more pronounced tail spikes unless pinned capacity is increased.
- Streaming mode: we stream token deltas to the client; post-stream latency per token once the stream is established is typically <50ms on our infra. We do not provide firm per-token SLA today, but we can set SLOs on per-chunk delivery rates for pilots.

Pilot runbook (short):
1) Confirm 5 representative prompts and 3 worst-case prompts (we’ll run both).
2) We provision a small dedicated pool (pin for no cold starts) + a shared fallback.
3) Redwood runs load tests: baseline, 1.5x sustained, 2x burst for 10m windows.
4) We provide a perf report and step-by-step failure modes.

I attached the raw perf CSV and a sample test script. Happy to run the SRE sync tomorrow at 10:30am PT if that works for Priya.

Attachments: redwood-perf-report-20260611.csv

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Technical Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. Quick decisions and next steps from our side:

- Decision criteria: if Redwood can demonstrate P99 < 600ms for our 5 representative prompts under a 1.5x sustained load with streaming enabled, we approve the pilot.
- Pilot timeline: aim to start the week of 2026-06-22 and run two weeks. Procurement is targeting an approval by 2026-06-20 if the pilot scope & costs look good.
- Security ask: Priya will send a short SOC2/evidence checklist; would prefer that in advance of procurement.

Priya — can you please drop the SOC2 checklist and any minimum evidence requirements in reply?

Marissa / Rishi / Vivek — please confirm availability for the SRE sync on Friday 2026-06-11 at 10:30am PT (if you ran the test earlier, we can move it earlier). Also confirm pilot pricing estimate so procurement can review.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Alex
